row.evidence: Mimecast's Incydr plan tables mark Identity management/SSO as available on every Incydr plan, and the SCIM article says Incydr creates, deactivates and updates users from any SCIM 2.0 provisioning provider; Incydr itself is sold only via Get a Quote.
row.notes: Quote-only: Code42 was acquired by Mimecast and Incydr is sold via 'Get a Quote' with no public tiers, so SCIM (included on all Incydr plans: Basic, Advanced, Professional, Enterprise, Gov F1/F2) can only be bought through sales. code42.com and support.code42.com now redirect to Mimecast; docs live in Mimecast's Zendesk help centre (cited via its JSON API because the HTML 403s bots). CrashPlan backup is now a separate company and is not covered. SCIM deactivation moves backup archives to cold storage and does not immediately free the licence. Also offers an LDAP-based Incydr User Directory Sync tool (via CSM). REST API has user list/get/activate/deactivate/role endpoints but no create; audit-log search API exists.

auth.token_source: Incydr console: Administration > Integrations > Identity Management > Provisioning > Add SCIM Provider (credential type API credentials = username/password, or OAuth token)
auth.notes: Two credential types: 'API credentials' (Base URL + username + password, required for Okta) or 'OAuth token' (bearer, required for Entra). Microsoft's tutorial calls it a long-lived bearer token; no expiry is documented. Shown once; 'Regenerate credentials' issues a new one.

operations.notes: Updates are documented (Okta and Entra overwrite Incydr values) but whether they arrive as PUT or PATCH is not.

deprovision.data_retained: Deactivation removes the user's account and moves their backup archives to cold storage (eventual deletion); a 15-minute default deactivation delay applies to provisioning (users are blocked immediately); users on legal hold are blocked instead of deactivated. Licences are not immediately freed while archives sit in cold storage.

custom.how: c42OrgName user attribute (managed in the IdP) maps users to Incydr organizations; no general custom-attribute support documented.

attributes.notes: Vendor list of provisionable attributes: first name, last name, title, division, department, employee type, manager, locality, region, country, external ID. Core/group names are from Microsoft's Entra tutorial mapping table. Manager from Okta needs Professional Services.

roles.how: Role mapping: Incydr roles assigned per SCIM group (requires SCIM groups); SCIM groups can also map users to organizations and watchlists.

limitations.text: Local Incydr users cannot be created, updated or deleted from the provisioning provider.
Okta provisioning needs Okta Lifecycle Management licensing.
SCIM groups are not supported for PingOne.
Okta Manager attribute requires Professional Services setup.

scim.notes: Base URL is generated per provider in Administration > Integrations > Identity Management > Provisioning > Add SCIM Provider; its pattern is not published. SSO and SCIM are separate settings ('If you want to add Okta as an authentication provider, see...'), and the docs never require SSO first, so sso_required is false by the docs' structure.

auth.notes: API client ID and secret exchanged at /v1/oauth for a 15-minute bearer token; basic auth is deprecated. Permissions are named per operation.

capabilities.notes: No create-user endpoint in the published OpenAPI; users come from SCIM, User Directory Sync, or the console. Directory groups are read-only (GET).

endpoints.purpose: Move a user to another organization

rate_limits.text: 120 API requests per minute; excess requests are blocked.

user_api.notes: Base API access comes with every plan; full access (all file-event metadata, file downloads) is included on Advanced/Enterprise/Gov and sold as an upgrade on Basic/Professional. The documented base/full differences concern file events and cases, not users, but the docs do not say outright that user endpoints are in base access, so api_tax stays null.

okta.notes: OIN 'Code42' app: SAML, SWA and SCIM with Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push and Group Linking checked (read from page markup). A separate 'Code42 Single Tenant' app exists.

google.notes: Vendor guide uses a custom SAML app in Google; no provisioning documented for Google.

onelogin.notes: Vendor guide adds the 'Code42 CrashPlan' app from OneLogin's catalogue for SAML SSO; provisioning not documented. OneLogin's own page not loaded.

jumpcloud.notes: JumpCloud support pages return 403 to plain requests; not checked.

fallbacks.other_sync: Incydr User Directory Sync (LDAP-based, configured with the CSM)
fallbacks.notes: SAML 2.0 SSO with any IdP (SP-initiated only).
